A well-established and diversified Saudi group is strengthening its Finance function as part of a wider growth and transformation programme and is looking to appoint experienced Senior

This opportunity is suited to technically strong, hands-on accountants who can demonstrate genuine General Ledger and month-end accounting ownership, alongside specialist experience within areas such as Accounts Receivable, Fixed Assets & Inventory and wider GL accounting.

This is not a transactional accounting position. We are looking for candidates who understand the accounting treatment behind transactions and can confidently explain and independently manage journals, accruals, reconciliations and period-end adjustments.
Take hands-on responsibility for General Ledger accounting and month-end close .
Prepare and post journals, accruals, prepayments and adjusting entries.
Perform and review balance-sheet and GL reconciliations , investigating and resolving discrepancies.
Ensure costs and revenues are recognised in the correct accounting period.
Support accounting activities across multiple sites, branches or business units .
Take specialist responsibility across areas such as AR, Fixed Assets, Inventory and/or other GL accounts.
Manage asset accounting including capitalisation, depreciation, CWIP, transfers and disposals where applicable.
Support inventory accounting including reconciliations, valuation, provisions, slow-moving/obsolete stock and adjustments.
Support AR accounting including invoicing, ageing, collections, reconciliations, provisions and month-end close where applicable.
Maintain strong financial controls, supporting schedules and audit-ready documentation.
Work closely with Operations, Procurement, Projects, Stores and other Finance teams.
6–8+ years of relevant accounting experience , with genuine Senior Accountant-level responsibility.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related financial discipline .
Strong hands-on General Ledger and month-end close experience .
Strong knowledge of accruals, prepayments, journals and balance-sheet reconciliations .
Ability to confidently explain the debit and credit treatment behind accounting transactions.
Strong understanding of the Chart of Accounts and Trial Balance .
Experience supporting multiple sites, branches, entities or business units – essential .
Strong ERP experience; SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics or similar preferred.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have personally dealt with complex accounting situations and can demonstrate why an accounting treatment was applied, rather than simply following an established process.

Experience across areas such as CWIP/project accounting, asset capitalisation, borrowing costs, inventory provisions, revenue/cost recognition, accruals and period-end adjustments will be particularly valuable.
Specific industry experience is not essential. The priority is strong technical accounting capability and experience operating across a complex, multi-site or multi-business environment.
At Salla, we are building the digital backbone of commerce in the region, for thousands of merchants starting, growing and scaling their businesses.

Catalog is the layer underneath everything: storefronts, search, recommendations and every channel a merchant sells through read from the same product data. This role owns both sides of that line, the catalog merchants build and the store their buyers shop.

Salla does not build the catalog. Merchants do, and often not even the merchant: a freelancer, operations staff, an agency. The buyer never sees the catalog, only whether they can find the product, trust the page and get what they ordered. Your job is to change what people who do not work for you produce, and turn that data into a store that converts. You lead four product managers across Catalog and Store, and you carry the numbers.
Areas of impact: product data input, structure and meaning, AI enrichment, store experience and search, and how the data performs downstream.
q: Six or more years in product management, including a self-serve platform where users created their own data and you owned its quality.
A number you moved by changing what users produced at the moment of entry, not by cleaning it up afterwards.
Hands-on ownership of a buyer-facing commerce experience, such as search, discovery or product pages, with conversion you moved and experiments that proved it.
AI in production on structured data, with concrete answers on confidence thresholds, error rates and what you did when it was wrong at scale.
Fluency in how product data is structured: taxonomies, attributes, variants, identifiers, matching, and external channel requirements.
You own outcomes rather than roadmaps, can set a strategy others repeat, and have managed and coached product managers without stepping away from the craft.
Full professional fluency in Arabic and English, regional merchant context preferred, and willing to work on-site in Saudi Arabia.
r: Set the strategy for Catalog and Store as one system, so a new category or way of selling is a configuration, not a rebuild.
Own how product data is created and improved, and define quality by how the data performs downstream, not by how many fields are filled.
Own the buyer's path from search to purchase: search relevance, the product page and availability.
Design for the people who actually enter the data, including those who do not own the store, so the good path is the fastest one.
Put AI to work where it earns trust: decide what we generate, what we suggest and what we never touch, and learn from every correction.
Use AI to take merchants from a blank store to a well-designed, ready-to-sell storefront.
Validate every bet against the outcome it promised: experiment where traffic allows, measure where it does not, and stop what does not work.
Decide how much structure to impose and where merchants stay free, including for external channels with strict requirements.
Lead four product managers, two on Catalog and two on Store: give them real ownership, coach their craft and raise the bar of what the group ships.
